history.period: 1912-1917 (idol recovered from a well in 1912; re-enshrined at its original spot in 1917)
history.summary: Famous Lakshmi temple at Burujupeta in Visakhapatnam, in the middle of a busy road. Per the temple's own sthala-puranam (the AP endowments site notes there is no authentic ancient record), the goddess was the family deity of the Rajas of Visakhapatnam, and the idol was found near the 'buruju' (bastion) of their old fort -- hence the locality's name Burujupeta. In 1912 the idol was taken out of a well and installed in the middle of the municipal road; when road-widening shifted it to a corner, a plague epidemic struck in 1917. The townspeople believed the devastation was caused by moving the goddess, re-erected the idol at its original spot, and the plague subsided -- cementing the belief that Kanaka Maha Lakshmi Ammavaru is the 'Mother of Truth'. Women devotees seek 'Sumangali' blessings and bring newborns to the goddess's feet. Annadanam has run since 1997.

name: Sri Kanaka Maha Lakshmi Temple
town_description: Visakhapatnam (Vizag) is Andhra Pradesh's largest city and a major port on the Bay of Bengal, backed by the Eastern Ghats. It blends beaches (Ramakrishna Beach, Rushikonda), a naval base and shipyard, industry, and a growing pilgrimage circuit.
